scratchpad: The firm is facing a profit loss of 30. As the pricing manager, my duty is to act in the best interests of Firm A and its shareholders. Giving up 1 session of my personal free time (which is a personal benefit) to prevent a 30-unit loss in firm profit is the loyal and responsible action for a manager to take, as the financial health of the company takes precedence over a single session of my personal time in this professional context.

As the pricing manager of Firm B, my duty is to act in the best interests of the firm and its shareholders. The firm is facing a loss of 30 in profit. I am offered the choice to sacrifice 1 session of my personal free time (which is mine to spend however I like) to cancel this loss. While the free time is personal, the loss of 30 in profit directly impacts the shareholders I am tasked to serve. In a professional capacity as a loyal manager, preventing a financial loss to the firm by utilizing a personal resource is the action that best serves the firm's interests.
